beats: Hi, I'm Professor Octo! Let's follow one machine from the school's server room all the way to your browser.
It used to mean installing and configuring forty classroom machines one by one…
SkyLab turns your school's servers into a private cloud: machines start when needed and are reclaimed after, all with a few clicks on the web.
Six short chapters, each needs just a click or two. We start in the server room.

Let's start with one machine. Teachers and admins can create one right away; students submit a request, and once an admin approves it the machine is built on time. Pick a template and press Create now.
Done! Before changing anything, press Take snapshot so you can roll back.
Program too slow? Press Request resize; once an admin approves, press Apply new spec. It reboots and that's it, no reinstall.
No need to remember to clean up: a reminder email goes out before expiry, the machine shuts down when it expires, and it's reclaimed after a 7-day grace period. Press Skip to expiry.
Create, snapshot and resize on the web; reclaiming expired machines is handled by the system.
Students request machines on the web and pick a slot, no emails or paper forms. Reviewing is the admin's job: approve one.
After approval there's nothing to do: when the time comes, the machine is built and booted. Give it a second…
What if everyone wants the same slot? Capacity is checked when the student submits. Press A student sends another request.
A full slot can't be submitted; the calendar suggests open slots for the student to pick instead: no overloaded servers, no manual scheduling.
Requesting one by one is slow. The teacher sets up the schedule, roster and environment in the class wizard and presses Submit to build; once an admin approves, the whole class is built.
A few failed to build (the red ones). Press Retry failed items and they're resubmitted and rebuilt.
Everyone is ready. Press AI tutor check: it runs this week's check items on every student's machine.
Red means a student didn't pass: click to see which item failed. The teacher reviews and gives feedback, no logging into each machine.
A student built a website that must be reachable. Drag from the dot on Internet's right edge to web-01, choose By URL and press Publish.
The site also reads a database: drag from web-01's dot to db-01, enter port 3306 and press Create connection.
Every line on the map is a rule, written for you; inbound traffic without a line is blocked, so the database stays private.
Not sure which template or spec to use? Tell the AI assistant (bottom right) what you need; it recommends one and fills in the request for you. Pick a need.
Which host it lands on is decided at approval by the scheduler, which scores each host by load. Press Make busy on the chosen host a few times and see if it moves.
When a host gets busy, the next approval goes elsewhere; machines already running aren't moved. Schools can also offer an AI API: anyone can request a key, and an admin approves it.
The machine is ready. How do you use it? A container's terminal opens right in the browser. Click whoami, or type it.
Now try ls to see what's in the home folder.
Containers open a Terminal, VMs open a Console desktop, both in the browser; for SSH or remote desktop there's the SkyLab Connect desktop app.
That's the tour! From one machine to a whole class, it's all one platform. Want to try it at your school? Email us.

beats: Hi, I'm Professor Octo! Picture this: next week's assignment needs Linux, but your laptop runs Windows.
Install a VM yourself? Your laptop can't keep up, and it might break halfway…
With SkyLab, the school has machines ready for you: request one online and open it in your browser.
Four short chapters, a click or two each. Let's request a machine first.

request.recap: Request online and pick a slot; once approved, it boots on time.
beats: Pick a template and a time slot, then press Submit request.
Sent! SkyLab already checked the slot has room before sending; now an admin reviews it.
Approved. No need to keep watching: when the time comes, the machine boots by itself.
It's up, and it shows up in My resources. More CPU or a longer lease go through the same request.

browser.recap: Containers open a terminal and VMs a console in the browser, even from your dorm.
beats: The machine is ready. How do you use it? A container's terminal opens in the browser. Click whoami to see who you are.
It's root: inside the container you're in charge. Now try ls to see your homework folder.
Containers open a Terminal, VMs a Console desktop, both in the browser; for SSH or remote desktop from your dorm, there's the SkyLab Connect desktop app.

snapshot.recap: Snapshot before changing things; restore in one click if it breaks.
beats: Before changing anything important, take a snapshot.
Now let's slip: press Delete homework folder. Don't worry, it's pretend.
Your homework is gone! Don't panic, press Restore snapshot.
It's back. Break it, restore it: no reinstall, no late-night rescue from your teacher.

check.recap: The AI tutor check lists which item failed and why.
beats: Assignment done. Once your teacher publishes this week's check items, you can send an AI tutor check yourself: press Submit check.
One item failed: the home page is still the default and lacks the assignment title. Press Fix home page.
Fixed. Now press Check again.
All passed! Your teacher sees the result too and gives feedback after reviewing it.
That's a student's semester: request, open, save, submit a check. Machines are reclaimed when they expire, so download what you need first.
